handoff.purpose: Render one council deliberation as markdown with structured sections.

symbols.name: render_verdict_markdown
symbols.note: Renders a council verdict into markdown string; no I/O or side effects.

claims.text: Order is deliberate and load-bearing: outcome and the quorum honesty line lead, so a degraded council is the first thing a reader sees and cannot be skimmed past.
claims.why: The code renders outcome (line 366) and quorum honesty (lines 393-406) at the top, before other sections.

claims.text: Then EVERY dissent verbatim with its author -- BEFORE the convergence, because the dissent is the only part that could not have come from asking one model twice.
claims.why: Dissent section (line 415) appears before convergence section (line 446).

claims.text: Then where the vendors converged, evidence digests, per-vendor cost/latency, the deliberation itself, and finally the provenance footer (bus path + chain head) that lets a reader verify all of it offline.
claims.why: The chunk ends at evidence digests (line 459); per-vendor cost/latency, deliberation, and provenance footer are not present in this chunk.

claims.text: Pure: no I/O, no network, no gate.
claims.why: The code in this chunk performs no I/O, but the claim refers to the entire function; cannot verify without seeing the rest of the function.

claims.text: CONVERGENCE, not 'majority'. A majority is a DECISION; convergence is an OBSERVATION about what the vendors said. The council package carries no approve/reject/score/majority/consensus field on purpose -- absence of the field is the control, not a docstring -- and a rendering that reintroduces the word structurally reintroduces the temptation to read it as a verdict. The legacy aliases are kept only so an older payload still renders.
claims.why: The comment references the council package's field design, which is not in this chunk.

claims.text: The advisory banner is UNCONDITIONAL. A verdict arriving without the marker is a contract violation, so we say so instead of quietly rendering it as if it carried authority.
claims.why: The code unconditionally adds advisory banner (lines 388-389) and then checks advisory field (lines 390-393).

claims.text: Quorum honesty, at the top. A short council is a weaker signal and that must be impossible to miss -- it is a warning block, not a footnote.
claims.why: Quorum section is placed after outcome and advisory, before dissents, and uses warning block for degraded quorum (lines 399-405).

claims.text: DISSENT LEADS. Not a stylistic choice: the dissent is the only content in this document that could not have been produced by asking one model twice. Convergence among vendors with overlapping training data is cheap; the objection is what four egress paths were actually paid for. Rendering it after -- and therefore below -- the agreement makes the informative half read as a footnote to the uninformative half.
claims.why: Dissent section (line 415) is rendered before convergence section (line 446).

claims.text: A vendor that did not speak has no content; an empty fence is noise that makes a silent turn look like an empty answer.
claims.why: Code only adds verbatim block if text is non-empty (lines 443-444).
